newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian Chernogorneft profit up, oil output down.
newsitem.headline: Russian Chernogorneft profit up, oil output down.

text.p: Russia's Chernogorneft oil producer saw 1996 net profit rise to $42.2 million, but its crude oil output slipped two percent to 8.93 million tonnes, a company statement said on Thursday.
* Figure is from the company's 1995 annual report.
Note -- Full name AO Chernogorneft. The company is a unit of NK SIDANKO (Sibirsko-Dalnevostochnaya Neftyanaya Kompaniya, a leading vertically-integrated oil major).
Its 1995 figures are cash-based, while 1996 figures are accruals-based; both are according to Russian accounting standards. Most of the figures are preliminary.

Chernogorneft said it paid lower taxes, excise duties and value-added tax in 1996, with all tax burdens consuming 25.5 percent of 1996 revenues compared to 31.8 percent in 1995. It said it benefited from a higher export quota and stronger world crude oil prices.
Chernogorneft said last year it planned a two percent rise in oil output in 1997.
Its level-one American Depositary Receipts are quoted on the NASDAQ bulletin board.
Chernogorneft has a joint venture with Occidental Petroleum of the United States.
